A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeMoA research. All 30 pages of v2 and 31 pages of v3, including figures, equations, tables, and Appendices A–E, support comparison. Isolated inconsistencies in experimental descriptions are qualified below.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original training-loss and accuracy results for MNIST/ConvNet and CIFAR-10/ResNet-18, including Byzantine attacks and non-Byzantine experiments.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments, including revised Byzantine-robustness curves and non-Byzantine CIFAR-10 results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 3.2 retain Bernoulli sampling, local momentum, decay of cached updates, and robust aggregation. Changing alpha to alpha_t in the pseudocode aligns it with v2's existing update equation. The revised theorem-specific stepsize restriction is assessed under T1.

E1.justification: MNIST, CIFAR-10, IID/non-IID classification, and the five plotted attack families remain. However, v3 removes non-Byzantine MNIST plots while Appendix B.2 still claims that evaluation. INF also disappears from configuration tables, although v2 provides no identifiable INF result. Whether actual scenario coverage narrowed is therefore unresolved.

E2.justification: The four optimizers remain, but aggregation comparison coverage substantially contracts. The naive-averaging attack comparisons in v2 Figure 6 disappear. CIFAR-10 loses the CM, Krum, and RFA comparisons from v2 Figures 7–9; v3 Table 3 specifies only CCLIP. Those aggregators remain evaluated on MNIST.

E3.justification: The main Byzantine CIFAR-10 experiment changes from 10 clients, including 2 Byzantine clients, and 200 epochs to 25 clients, including 5 Byzantine clients, and 1000 epochs. Figure 2 switches from participation 0.1 to the previously covered 0.5 setting. Reported momentum coverage contracts from 0.9/0.99 to 0.9. These substantially revise experimental settings.

E4.justification: V2 Figures 3 and 4 examine non-Byzantine performance across participation rates 0.1/0.5 and momentum values 0.9/0.99 on both datasets. V3 removes these matrices and retains only the CIFAR-10 example at participation 0.5 and momentum 0.9, substantially reducing sensitivity evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions use seeds {0,1,2}, select configurations by mean validation accuracy, and describe shaded regions as standard deviations across seeds. No changed repetition count or statistical reporting procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Numerous curves change and appendix result panels disappear. Under the revised CIFAR-10 settings, v3 Figure 1b shows Byz-VR-MARINA-PP above DeMoA for IID ALIE, reversing the ranking in v2's corresponding panel. Changed client counts and training horizons prevent interpreting this as a same-setting performance change. Retained MNIST plots also contain revised trajectories.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 replaces the explicit lower bound on honest-client count G with a Gamma-dependent stepsize cap and revises the finite-time bound; Corollary 3.2 changes accordingly. Appendix E.3 revises the supporting argument and adds Lemma E.9 with a stepsize-tuning proof, including the b=0 case. This substantially changes the central theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: cached momentum prevents Byzantine-majority aggregation, DeMoA adds no communication overhead, convergence is guaranteed under stated conditions, and experiments support robustness under partial participation. Their substantive scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds discussion distinguishing worst-case theoretical robustness from incomplete empirical coverage of adaptive attacks targeting delayed momentum. It also identifies server memory at scale as a limitation and discusses compression as future work. The discussion defending a minimum honest-client count is removed following the theorem revision.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.5 specifies the aggregators and discloses CCLIP's three iterations, threshold 10.0, and initialization from the previous aggregate, plus Krum's stated 18-neighbor selection. These are newly documented implementation details, without evidence that those settings changed. Hardware, software versions, and the referenced implementation codebase remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 expands the cached-update comparison beyond MIFA to FedVARP and CA2FL, adds the corresponding citations, and introduces a compression discussion citing Khirirat et al. Existing research positioning largely remains; removing the duplicated Blanchard reference does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: V3 makes targeted explanatory and related-work revisions, adds an aggregator-definition subsection, and updates affiliations, acknowledgments, and conference boilerplate. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The appendix presentation is substantially reorganized: the non-Byzantine matrices and naive-averaging figure are removed, CM/Krum/RFA figures lose their CIFAR-10 panels, and extended plots move before the proofs. Figure 1b's epoch axis expands to 1000. V3 Figure 3b also introduces a caption conflict by labeling a 200-epoch panel as MNIST.

improvement.justification: The revised theorem relaxes the stated client-count requirement, and the explicit stepsize proof and aggregator settings improve theoretical exposition and reproducibility. However, v3 removes useful sensitivity and cross-aggregator evidence, while Figure 3b conflicts with the documented MNIST protocol and revised rankings receive little interpretive adjustment. These material benefits and losses do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
